questions.question: Power steering hoses should be checked for:

options.text: Whether they are connected to the battery.
Whether they have the proper amount of play.

questions.explanation: Check power steering hoses, pumps, and fluid levels. Look specifically for leaks in the hoses.

questions.question: Before a trip, test the tractor protection valve by:

options.text: Releasing air by pressing the brake pedal.
Releasing air by pressing the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Releasing air by pressing the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Let the air system charge fully. Turn off the engine. Press the brake pedal several times to release air from the system. The tractor protection valve should move to its emergency position when air pressure drops too low.

questions.question: When ice on the road begins to melt as temperatures rise:

options.text: It is especially safe to drive.
It is easier to identify slippery spots.

questions.explanation: Wet, melting ice is much more slippery than dry ice. Drive with extra caution when ice is melting.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights and fog lights in fog to see better. High beam lights will reflect off the fog and make it harder to see.

questions.question: During a trip, which shut-off valves should be open?

options.text: All shut-off valves except the rear ones.

questions.correctAnswerText: All shut-off valves except the rear ones.
questions.explanation: Open all shut-off valves except the rear ones on the last trailer. This lets air reach all the brakes while preventing air from escaping out the back of the vehicle.

questions.question: What does the air compressor governor do?

options.text: Controls when the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.
Controls how fast air leaves the storage tanks.
Controls the temperature of air entering the storage tanks.
Controls the temperature of air leaving the storage tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Controls when the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor controls when the compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.

questions.question: When checking automatic transmission fluid, the vehicle:

options.text: Should be lifted with a jack.

questions.explanation: The engine may need to be running to check the automatic transmission fluid level.

questions.question: Move over laws require drivers to:

options.text: Move to a lane away from the stopped emergency vehicle.
Move to the far side of their lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a lane away from the stopped emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is stopped on a multilane road, move to a different lane if possible. If you cannot move over safely, slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.question: Which is NOT a sign of damaged brakes?

options.text: Shoes with oil or grease on them.
Pads free of oil or grease.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pads free of oil or grease.
questions.explanation: Signs of brake problems include cracked drums; shoes or pads with oil, grease, or brake fluid on them; and shoes that are missing, broken, or worn too thin. Pads free of oil or grease are good.

questions.question: Test the low pressure warning signal:
questions.explanation: Test the low pressure warning light before every trip. After the system charges, press and release the brake pedal rapidly to release air. The warning signal should come on when pressure drops to a dangerous level.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT part of an air brake system?
questions.explanation: Air brakes have three separate systems: the service brake system, the parking brake system, and the emergency brake system.

questions.question: If you meet an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Try to get out of their way.

questions.explanation: When facing an aggressive driver, get out of their way. Do not make eye contact. Do not react to their gestures. Do not speed up to challenge them.

questions.question: If you lose hydraulic brake pressure, do all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: If you lose hydraulic brake pressure, downshift, pump the brakes, and use the parking brake. Look for an escape route such as an escape ramp, open field, or side street.

questions.question: If you unlock the pintle hook before pulling the dolly out from under the rear trailer, what can happen?

options.text: The tow bar may cause injury.

questions.correctAnswerText: The tow bar may cause injury.
questions.explanation: Always pull the dolly out from under the rear trailer before unlocking the pintle hook. If you don't, the dolly tow bar could fly up and cause serious injury.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a good rule for using turn signals?

options.text: Do not use your turn signal if you think others know what you plan to do.
Cancel your signal after the turn is completed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use your turn signal if you think others know what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Always signal when you plan to turn or change lanes. Signal well before you turn. Keep signaling during the entire turn. Turn off your signal when the turn is finished.

questions.question: When you start a vehicle, warning lights and buzzers should:

options.text: Turn off within a few seconds.
Stay on until you turn them off manually.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off within a few seconds.
questions.explanation: After the engine starts, warning lights and buzzers for oil, coolant, charging circuits, and the Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) should turn off right away.

questions.question: To release a dolly's air brakes before coupling it to the rear trailer, you should:

options.text: Remove the dolly parking brake control.

questions.explanation: To release a converter dolly's air brakes, open the air tank petcock. This is the first step when positioning the dolly in front of the rear trailer.

questions.question: Compared to empty rigs, fully-loaded rigs are:

options.text: Just as likely to roll over.

questions.explanation: Fully-loaded rigs have a higher center of gravity due to the weight of the cargo. They are 10 times more likely to roll over in a crash than empty rigs.

questions.question: If a vehicle has an inspection report, the driver should:

options.text: Not look at the report and find any issues themselves.
Take the vehicle to a mechanic.
Skip the pre-trip inspection and only use the report.

questions.explanation: As the first step of vehicle inspection, review the last inspection report. The carrier should have fixed any problems listed on the report.

questions.question: What happens if one-fourth of the leaves are missing from a leaf spring during an inspection?

options.text: The driver may drive, but only at reduced speeds.
The vehicle will be put out-of-service until it is fixed.
The vehicle is fine to drive since most of the spring is still there.
The driver will be asked to reduce the load weight.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle will be put out-of-service until it is fixed.
questions.explanation: If one-fourth or more of the leaves are missing from a leaf spring, the vehicle will be put out-of-service until the problem is fixed.
